newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhtelekom searches for 1.5 bln-mark investor.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhtelekom searches for 1.5 bln-mark investor.

text.p: The chairman of Kazakhstan's telecoms monopoly, unruffled by a failed deal with Deutsche Telekom AG, said on Tuesday a 40 percent stake offered to foreign investors would raise the concern 1.5 billion marks ($887.3 million).

"We hope that by the end of March one of these companies will be granted an exclusive right to lead direct negotiations with the government," Kazakhtelekom Chairman Serik Burkitbayev told Reuters in an interview.
Burkitbayev said the winner will be announced next month and would be expected to invest about 1.5 billion marks.

Four companies, including Korea's Daewoo Telecom Co Ltd and France's Alcatel, are bidders in the tender for the stake in NAK Kazakhtelekom announced in January, a government official told Reuters on condition of anonymity.
A framework agreement signed in 1996 between Kazakhtelekom and Deutsche Telekom for a 49-percent stake in the monopoly and the right to manage the concern collapsed in January.
Deutsche Telekom had planned to increase the oil-rich republic's 2.1 million telephone lines to 4.5 million within 10 years.
But Kazakh officials cancelled the deal, saying Deutsche Telekom was not ready to invest the agreed amount.

Burkitbayev said the investor who wins the current tender will not have the right to manage Kazakhtelekom. The state currently owns 90 percent of the shares, with the remaining 10 percent held by the workforce.
"Of course, the investor will have to share with us the responsibility for our debts, to be paid by the year 2004," he said.
Burkitbayev said Kazakhtelekom had already paid off 100 million marks out of 520 million it owed to German investment agency Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau for a 1992 loan.
The expected investment of 1.5 billion marks includes the share of debt to be paid off by the investor, he said.
"But the remaining 420 million marks is not a critical sum for a company such as Kazakhtelekom," he said.
Burkitbayev said Kazakhtelekom needed a clear-cut investment strategy for the next 10-15 years.
"What we need at the moment is to bring telephone lines closer to international standards and to make efficient use of Kazakhstan's advantageous geographical position," he said.
Kazakhtelekom aims to plough foreign investment into boosting the number of telephone lines in the country, with a population of 16.9 million, to five million within the next decade.
"Besides, Kazakhstan could earn hundreds of millions dollars a year as it lies in the centre of Eurasia and is a communications hub between Europe and Asia," Burkitbayev said.
Burkitbayev said the government might sell part of the 50-percent stake it will retain after the tender on the former Soviet republic's nascent stock market at the end of the year.
